newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam President conscious after stroke--sources.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam President conscious after stroke--sources.

text.p: Vietnamese President Le Duc Anh has regained consciousness after suffering a stroke and has asked to be allowed to return to work, Vietnaese political sources said on Sunday.
But one of the sources, who declined to be named, said doctors were not optimistic that 75-year-old General Anh would recover sufficiently to carry on as president.

Government officials earlier confirmed that Anh had been admitted to Hanoi's 108 Army hospital on Friday. But there have been widely varying reports of his condition since admission and an official veil of secrecy has been drawn across the situation.

One source said on Sunday evening that Anh had been paralysed down one side of his body by haemorrhaging around the brain, which was at odds with the comment of a medical worker earlier that his condition had improved and he might be discharged soon.

Anh is a key figure in the communist country's leadership triumvirate, a collective system comprising three powerful figures chosen to ensure balance between different shades of socialist opinion and differing regional views.

He is viewed by Western observers as the most conservative of the trio. The other two are Communist Party chief Do Muoi, 79, who is seen as occupying a central and stabilising role in government, and reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, 73.
